messages:
omar (Sales): Quick question about per-diem/prorating at a multi-city conference. Traveled Mon-Wed: stayed in City A Mon-Tue, then moved to City B Tue night-Wed. Company covers hotel + per-diem but City A is high-cost and City B is low-cost. I was reimbursed for hotel nights but my per-diem got flagged. What rule applies for prorating when you switch cities mid-trip?
alesha (People Ops): For multi-city same trip we use per-diem by overnight location. So nights physically spent in City A use City A per-diem, nights in City B use City B rate. If you change hotels after midnight, we use the calendar night of the stay.
omar (Sales): Ok that makes sense. My treasurer put all meals on one daily line and used City A rate for both Tue and Wed because travel started there. Is that wrong?
frank (Finance): We need the per-diem broken down by date and city. Expense form field: `Per-diem breakdown (dates/city/rate)`. If you combined them, please edit the entry and attach the hotel folios that show the check-in/check-out dates.
tara (Manager): I approved the trip originally. Confirming Omar slept in City B on Tue night.
omar (Sales): Yes I checked out of City A on Tue afternoon and arrived City B by 9pm, stayed overnight.
alesha (People Ops): Also reminder: per-diem caps are region-based. If City A has a higher cap and you used same-day meals in City B that were more expensive, Finance will request receipts for individual meals exceeding the cap.
frank (Finance): If any single meal > per-diem single-meal threshold for that city, we require receipt and will reimburse actual up to reasonableness. Otherwise we reimburse the standard per-diem amount for the night.
omar (Sales): What about a client dinner in City B that was split between personal + company? We paid with my personal card for alcohol and client paid their portion separately. I only asked for company share.
alesha (People Ops): For shared meals, include the itemized receipt, highlight the company portion, and add a short note `Shared meal with client — company portion $X`. Manager approval required for client entertainment.
frank (Finance): If alcohol is included and company policy disallows alcohol as a separate line unless pre-approved, mark the line and get manager sign-off. In practice we usually reimburse food; alcohol is discretionary and may be capped.
omar (Sales): Got it. One more wrinkle: City B is in a different country. I tipped in cash for taxis and meals. Do we accept cash tip receipts?
alesha (People Ops): Cash tips: take a photo of the receipt or annotate the receipt with the tip amount if it isn't printed. If no receipt exists, submit a short attestation with approximate amounts and manager approval. Keep entries reasonable.
expenses-bot: Reminder: upload photos as PNG or PDF <5MB. Use Expense ID in notes.
omar (Sales): I've edited the expense and added per-diem breakdown + hotel folios + client meal receipt. Expense ID: EXP-2112345.
frank (Finance): Receipt set looks better. We'll clear the flag after manager confirmation on alcohol line. Expect processing in ~3 business days.
tara (Manager): Confirmed — alcohol portion not company-covered beyond $25. Approving remaining amount.
omar (Sales): Thanks everyone :raised_hands: This is super helpful for future trips.
expenses-bot: Files received. Expense EXP-2112345 pending final review.
